primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A stable project-controlled identifier for a semantic subject or independently governed unit when continuity or reference across carriers or revisions materially matters; it is not a path, title, provider identity, or Git blob.

seams.meaning_statement: Knowledge and AO must refer to the same governing semantic subject when resolving authority and reconstructing control context.
AO and WARRANT-F need a common subject identity so admission evaluates the semantic object AO intends to advance.
AO and workstream continuity need stable identities for referenced workstreams and execution bindings even when branch or path carriers change.
Collaboration session and thread identifiers are domain identities and may reference semantic subjects without becoming the same global semantic-identity primitive.
AO and transition management must preserve the identity of subjects and control cycles across successor bridging.
Transition and Engineering or Delivery need the same target subject identity so realization and evidence attach to the intended object rather than a carrier accident.
Knowledge and retrieval or navigation require identity continuity independent of file path.
Assurance evidence must identify the semantic subject it supports independently of storage or provider location.
Evolution cases must preserve the identity of the affected semantic owner across amendments, supersession, and historical retention.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: An explicit binding that identifies both the governed semantic subject and the exact repository or content revision or accepted base against which a consequential decision, action, evidence item, or reconstruction result is valid.

seams.meaning_statement: Authority resolution and reconstruction must bind the governing sources and revisions actually used.
AO and WARRANT-F must agree on exact subject and revision and applicable base policy before admission.
Workstream and Git decisions require exact precondition revision or ref state so AO does not act on stale execution context.
Collaboration continuity requires a durable project anchor so a handoff or restart refers to the exact known project boundary.
Bridge authority resolution explicitly binds exact revision and freshness before consequential action.
Transition and Engineering evidence must bind the exact source subject and revision being migrated, qualified, or delivered.
Retrieval and reconstruction must preserve source revision and freshness rather than treating latest search result as authority.
Assurance and evidence delivery require exact subject and revision binding for decision-grade evidence.
Architecture evolution must name the affected contract or semantic owner and exact revision.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A non-authoritative descriptor sufficient to trace a project fact, control record, evidence item, handoff, or generated result to its relevant source or materialization identity and origin, without inferring authority from transport or location.

seams.meaning_statement: Knowledge and AO reconstruction need inspectable origin and source bindings for the context used to resolve authority.
AO and WARRANT-F need provenance and trust context for decision-grade assurance without making execution surface authority.
Workstream and Git continuity rely on exact pre and post Git state and publication receipts as provenance.
Collaboration continuity explicitly preserves interaction and session provenance and durable anchors.
Bridge receipts need inspectable control-cycle, authority, and execution provenance while remaining non-authoritative evidence.
Engineering and Delivery must publish exact, immutable or content-addressable evidence whose origin can be resolved independently of one CI UI.
Retrieval and navigation must preserve where a result came from so a derived route cannot masquerade as governing authority.
Assurance and evidence delivery explicitly depend on exact evidence identity, immutability, and provenance.
Evolution cases record trigger sources and observed evidence so dispositions remain auditable without retroactive rewriting.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A reference to the normative lifecycle or effective state of a governing semantic unit, sufficient to distinguish proposal, current effect, withheld effect, supersession, retirement, and rejection without confusing those states with operational workstream or bridge state.

seams.meaning_statement: Knowledge and AO must distinguish current governing sources from superseded or historical material during authority resolution.
AO and WARRANT-F must evaluate against effective accepted or base policy rather than stale or merely proposed policy.
Workstream lifecycle state is domain control state, not the same primitive as governing normative lifecycle.
Collaboration or thread lifecycle may reference governing objects but its session states need not become governing lifecycle.
Successor transition must distinguish current authority, prospective successor semantics, and historical authority without laundering control state into authority.
Engineering and Delivery may realize only accepted or effective governing changes and must preserve the transition from accepted design to activation.
Navigation and current orientation must not present superseded or historical governing material as current authority.
Assurance evidence must be interpreted against the governing policy and revision actually effective for the decision.
AO-4 explicitly governs proposal, keep, amend, supersede, reopen, and historical acceptance semantics.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A stable reference to an accepted or activated project obligation together with its governing source and revision, allowing control, workstream, transition, realization, and reconstruction records to refer to the same obligation without duplicating its normative text.

seams.meaning_statement: Knowledge and reconstruction and AO share activated obligations and closure conditions.
WARRANT-F consumes effective claims and policy for admission; generic obligation identity need not become claim-internal assurance semantics.
AO and workstream routing convert project obligations into concrete lifecycle obligations and must preserve which obligation is discharged.
Collaboration continuity must preserve pending review and handoff obligations across interaction boundaries without promoting chat to authority.
Bridge receipts explicitly carry activated obligations while current authority remains authoritative.
Accepted architecture and evolution obligations must link to implementation or migration, evidence, qualification, and activation.
Reconstruction must load mandatory control obligations and deferred triggers by reference to authoritative sources rather than copied prose.
Assurance evidence is natively related to claims and warrants; forcing generic project-obligation identity into evidence internals would over-unify the assurance domain.
AO-4 makes prospective realization obligations explicit outputs of accepted evolution dispositions.

primitive_annotations.canonical_meaning: A typed, source-owned reference from one semantic unit to another with explicit target and scope when needed, where the relation meaning is governed and reverse or closure views may be derived rather than becoming duplicate authority.

seams.meaning_statement: Authority and reconstruction need governed semantic relations such as replace, supplement, specialize, and correct to resolve governing scope.
AO and WARRANT-F can use exact request and result references without making assurance claim and warrant internals part of a generic relation registry.
Workstream and Git execution bind workstream, integration boundary, and exact Git state without making branch path semantic authority.
Collaboration can reference workstreams, routes, and handoffs through bounded collaboration records without sharing all thread relations globally.
Successor bridging depends on explicit predecessor, successor, and current-authority relationships rather than implicit file precedence.
Accepted change must relate governing source, realization target, evidence, and qualification without duplicating authority.
Knowledge navigation relies on semantic relationships distinct from physical parentage and source-owned rather than centrally registered membership.
Evidence-to-claim and warrant relationships are assurance-domain semantics; provenance and exact subject binding are sufficient at the shared seam.
Evolution and supersession need governed relations that preserve predecessor and successor scope while historical authority remains reconstructable.

negative_controls.rationale: The exact open, paused, resumed, or current workstream state belongs to the workstream and control domain. AO, continuity, and transition may reference it without owning or duplicating its state machine in the shared substrate.
Bridge mode is transition-control state. AO and authority resolution need bridge outputs and membrane guarantees, not a globally shared execution-mode ontology.

Claim and warrant evaluation internals are owned by WARRANT-F. AO shares exact subject and consequence and consumes the decision envelope; importing claim-internal state would collapse the assurance boundary.
Sampling statistics are assurance and evaluation evidence internals. Other domains need the qualified decision or evidence reference, not campaign-statistic semantics themselves.

status_label_assessment.assessment: The six provisional labels are semantically usable at unit scope. EFFECT_WITHHELD is preferable to HELD or SUSPENDED because it reduces collision with AO affected-scope holds, workstream pause, and bridge SUSPENDED. It should mean only that a governing unit is accepted or governing in principle while operational effect is deliberately not yet effective for a declared scope. SUPERSEDED and RETIRED remain distinct: superseded preserves a successor relation; retired means no longer operationally applicable without implying semantic replacement.
